selector.inherited_order: minimum (codec_rank, source_index, codec) per logical target, then product post-filter to allowed_inverse_codecs

theorem: A disallowed candidate may be skipped before decode only when its known codec rank is strictly worse than every known allowed codec rank. If any allowed codec is unknown/unranked, pruning is disabled. The rule preserves the inherited minimum-rank/source-index winner before the existing post-filter.
proof_sketch: If the baseline winner is allowed, every skipped candidate has worse codec rank and cannot outrank it.
If the baseline winner is disallowed but not rank-dominated, it remains visible and continues to mask later allowed candidates.

If the baseline winner is disallowed and rank-dominated, no allowed candidate can be present: any present allowed candidate would have lower rank and would already have won. Removing the dominated winner therefore still yields no allowed edge.
Same-codec source-index ordering is untouched because pruning operates only by codec class and never removes an allowed codec.
shipping_consequence: For current allowed={gzip,zstd}, xz is the only recognized codec that is rank-safe to skip before decode.
negative_control: With allowed={gzip}, zstd is disallowed but rank 0. If zstd and gzip both match, full discovery selects zstd and the post-filter emits no edge. Blind unsupported-codec skipping would incorrectly expose gzip.
implementation_boundary: Full discovery remains default for research callers when allowed_inverse_codecs is omitted.
The existing V2 post-filter remains the semantic authority after prospective pruning.
Unknown allowed codec ranks disable pruning conservatively.
Skipped-sidecar telemetry is build evidence only and must not alter archive bytes.
claim_boundary: Selector derivation/property evidence only. Exact-head implementation tests, hostile supported/disallowed codec cases, hosted same-input product A/B and unchanged external gates remain mandatory before product/release credit.
